Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Immediate localized reaction at arm sting site with mild redness and puncture mark; no notable local swelling. Video exam shows normal breathing and speech; no visible lip/oropharyngeal swelling. Patient anxious, reports subjective dyspnea and oral sensations. No GI symptoms, syncope, hives, wheeze, or stridor reported.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting: Most consistent with localized erythema and stable exam.
  - Early anaphylaxis: Considered due to temporal relationship and subjective dyspnea/oral sensations; no objective airway or systemic involvement during consult.
  - Anxiety-related dyspnea (hyperventilation): Possible contributor given history and normal observed respiration.
- Working diagnosis: Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp). Monitor for progression to systemic reaction.
- Management priorities: Symptomatic control with antihistamines; education on red flags for anaphylaxis; safety-netting for urgent care if deterioration. Consider bacterial infection only if spreading erythema, warmth, pain, or systemic features develop.

Management Plan

- Start oral antihistamine: chlorphenamine 4 mg up to six times daily or a once-daily non-sedating alternative (OTC).
- Safety netting: Seek urgent care/emergency department immediately for any lip/tongue/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, wheeze/stridor, voice change, dizziness/syncope, rapidly spreading rash, or any symptom progression.
- Local site care: Observe. If redness spreads, area becomes hot/tender, or systemic signs occur, reassessment for possible antibiotics.
- Education: Provided information on signs/symptoms of anaphylaxis and when to seek emergency care.
- Follow-up: Return or telehealth review if symptoms persist, worsen, or if recurrent reactions occur; consider allergy evaluation if recurrent or systemic reactions develop.
  
- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting – High likelihood. Justification: Immediate localized erythema with puncture mark; no objective airway involvement; stable exam.
- Early anaphylaxis (IgE-mediated) – Moderate likelihood. Justification: Temporal proximity to sting with subjective dyspnea and oral sensations; however no visible swelling, normal breathing, no systemic features.
- Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea – Moderate likelihood. Justification: History of anxiety/panic; normal observed respiration and speech; anxiety after sting may explain dyspnea sensation.
